struck: Horry's homes are younger than most.
use: Horry's homes are younger than the state's and the nation's.

pattern: \b2000 (?:to|and|through) 2009\b[^.]{0,80}\b(?:the )?(?:largest|most|biggest) (?:of any|share of any)? ?decade\b|\blargest of any decade\b
struck: About 1 in 5 Horry County homes (20.5 percent) were built from 2000 to 2009, the largest of any decade.
use: About 1 in 5 Horry County homes (20.5 percent) were built from 2000 to 2009, about as many as from 2010 to 2019.

struck: Homes built before 1972 and wired with aluminum were 55 times more likely to have a connection reach "fire hazard conditions" than homes wired with copper.
use: A national survey done for the CPSC found that homes built before 1972 and wired with aluminum were 55 times more likely to have a wire connection at an outlet reach "fire hazard conditions" than homes wired with copper.

struck: These are averages for standard quality "under average conditions", not a date a part fails.
use: These are HUD's recommended average lives, not a date a part fails.

struck: The Grand Strand's air conditioners work almost twice as hard as Columbus, Ohio's and about 1.6 times as hard as New York City's.
use: The North Myrtle Beach airport averages about twice the cooling degree days of Columbus, Ohio, and about 1.6 times New York City's.

struck: South Carolina's is the official wood infestation report (the CL-100).
use: South Carolina's is the Official South Carolina Wood Infestation Report, the report people here call the CL-100.

struck: A house the appraiser rates C6 cannot be financed until it is repaired to at least C5.
use: Fannie Mae does not buy a loan on a house rated C6. Those problems must be fixed, to at least C5, before Fannie Mae buys the loan.

struck: The most used form, written by Florida's state-run insurer, asks for the roof's age.
use: A sample form from Citizens Property Insurance, a Florida insurer, asks for the roof's age.

struck: The form asks the age of the heating and air system and its last service.
use: The form asks the age of the heating and air system and the year it was last updated, with a photo of its dated data plate.

pattern: \bnew roof (?:is a permitted job|in the county comes with a permit)\b|\bevery roof (?:repair|job) needs a permit\b
struck: In unincorporated Horry County, a new roof is a permitted job.
use: Horry County's roof certification letter asks for the job's permit number and a notarized statement that the roof covering and underlayment were attached for high-wind areas under the 2021 South Carolina Residential Code.

struck: The report covers termites and other wood-destroying insects anywhere, and rot below the main floor.
use: The report covers termites and other wood-destroying insects in every part the inspector can see and reach, and rot below the main floor.

struck: The report must list all damage, even damage that was repaired before.
use: The report must list all damage, even damage left in places that were repaired before.

struck: It is not a warranty, and it does not require anyone to fix what it finds.
use: It is not a warranty, and it does not oblige the pest company to fix what it finds.

struck: An owner who knowingly gives false, incomplete or misleading information on the statement is liable to the buyer for actual damages and court costs, and a court may add attorney fees.
use: An owner who knowingly gives false, incomplete or misleading information on the statement can owe the buyer actual damages and court costs, and a court may add the winner's attorney fees.

pattern: \bSouth Carolina law does not (?:make|require) a seller (?:to )?(?:fix|repair)\b
struck: South Carolina law does not make a seller fix anything before a sale.
use: South Carolina's disclosure law does not require a seller to make repairs.

pattern: \brecommended to sellers were cheap\b|\bmost often recommended[^.]{0,40}\bcheap\b
struck: In NAR's 2025 survey of agents, the fixes most often recommended to sellers were cheap: declutter (91 percent).
use: In NAR's 2025 survey of agents, the fixes most often recommended to sellers were to declutter (91 percent).

pattern: \brepairs, which do not go into your (?:home's )?basis\b
struck: For tax, the IRS treats painting and fixing leaks as repairs, which do not go into your home's basis.
use: For tax, the IRS treats painting and fixing leaks as repairs, which do not go into your basis unless they are done as part of a larger remodeling job.

struck: Among houses built 2016 or later, fewer than 1 in 100 do.
use: Among houses built 2016 or later, about 1 in 100 do.

pattern: \bmost newer houses here sit on a slab\b
struck: Most newer houses here sit on a slab.
use: Most newer houses for sale here list a slab foundation.

struck: Houses for sale built 2005 or earlier that advertise a new roof had cut their price about as often as, or more often than, those that do not.
use: (cut it: the price-cut comparison is mixed by band and is not for the page)

pattern: \b(?:its )?full name is the Official South Carolina Wood Infestation Report\b
struck: Its full name is the Official South Carolina Wood Infestation Report.
use: It is written on the state's form, the Official South Carolina Wood Infestation Report.

struck: It is a rough clock, not a date a part fails.
use: It is an average. A roof can last longer or fail sooner.

use: (cut: a Florida rule; the page names no insurer's age rule until OWNER-QUESTIONS Q2 is answered)

use: We found no roof age limit in South Carolina's insurance laws.

struck: An insurer that asks for a four-point inspection gets the roof's age and its years of life left from the report.
use: Insurers can still ask about the roof. The sample four-point form from Citizens, a Florida insurer, asks for the roof's age and its years of life left.
